page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn6e-c12g1.12xlarge is a GPU-accelerated server instance designed for workloads requiring parallel processing capabilities. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor with 48 vCPUs and 24 physical cores running at 2.5 GHz, this x86_64 architecture instance features dedicated CPU allocation. The hardware configuration includes 368.0 GB of system memory, providing 7.67 GB per core. Acceleration is delivered via four integrated NVIDIA Volta V100 GPUs, offering a combined total of 128 GB of VRAM. This instance does not include local storage, relying on network-attached storage options, and features a baseline network bandwidth of 16 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates moderate multi-core and memory performance alongside weaker single-core metrics. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance score is 35520.27, which is categorized as average, whereas the single-core CPU score of 1110.4 is weak. Memory bandwidth testing shows average throughput, reaching 1975.99 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 98.85 GB/sec for large-block reads. Single-threaded operations show limitations, with a poor gzip compression rate of 19.36 GB/sec and a weak bzip3 decompression rate of 7.68 GB/sec. However, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression scales to an average tier of 147.7 GB/sec. Database and web serving capabilities are stable, with Redis SET operations achieving 33.18 million operations per second and static web serving throughput reaching 23.02 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.gn6e-c12g1.12xlarge represents a high-density resource profile where the primary value lies in the quad-GPU configuration and substantial memory capacity rather than raw single-core CPU speed. The absence of local storage requires external storage provisioning, which should be factored into architectural planning. This server is best suited for GPU-accelerated workloads such as deep learning training, parallel scientific computing, high-performance data analysis, and multi-threaded processing tasks that can leverage the Volta architecture and the 128 GB of total VRAM.
